title: B-2: panel sort, archive listings and plug-in services keep the old comparison
reason: maintainer 2026-10-04: the remaining B-2 systemic work is not implemented - it changes what users see (panel order, archive and plug-in listings) or what plug-ins get, with the highest regression risk for a mostly theoretical gain; every identity decision that could lose data was converted (092) and the losses found since were fixed one by one (103, 107-110, 112, 113, 115, 117, 119). Re-open only with a concrete wrong-file or lost-data scenario.
problem: The remainder of encoding cluster B-2 would move the last name comparisons to the file system's rule: (1) the panel sort comparator, which is intransitive with "Use locale" off for names mixing ASCII and other characters (found by the 092 research); (2) `CSalamanderDirectory` (archive and plug-in listings), which compares names by the byte fold with a case-sensitive mode chosen by the plug-in; (3) the comparison services exported to plug-ins (`StrICmp`, `IsTheSamePath`, `SalParsePath`, `PathsAreOnTheSameVolume`, ...), which keep the byte fold; (4) a guard rule for the old comparison functions. The merged `Dir`/`DIR` folders of ZIP/TAR listings (queue 108, entry 4: tar extracts case-sensitively under a case-insensitive listing, so a Linux tarball with `Dir/a.txt` and `DIR/b.txt` shows one merged `Dir`) follow the `CSalamanderDirectory` listing and would move with it - no loss known.
evidence: Decision: specs/NEXT-WORK.md item 5, *Decision (maintainer, 2026-10-04): the remaining B-2 systemic work is NOT implemented* (L1317 at 7993914c) and the four entries below it (L1328-1340); queue 108 entry 4 at L1495 (`plugins/tar/untar.cpp:330`, `strcmp`). Core identity done by feature 092 (`specs/092-name-identity-unicode/fix-log.md`); disk-cache keys done by 109. Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §C *Decided - not to do* (L470, at 7993914c).
notes: The comparator's cost (item 5, *The comparator's cost*, still open, low) and queue 108 entry 4's other remarks belong to other parts of the migration (item 5 / Open items at a glance).
log: maintainer: the remaining B-2 systemic work (panel sort comparator, CSalamanderDirectory comparison, plug-in comparison services, guard rule) is not implemented

title: A plug-in's Save dialog may open the program's last folder, not the panel's
reason: feature 121, 2026-10-06 (listed under NEXT-WORK §C Decided - not to do): measured as Windows' per-program first-folder rule, by design; putting the folder into `lpstrFile` did not change it; only `IFileDialog::SetFolder` would - a change of API, a feature of its own if wanted. The 121 change was reverted.
problem: Checksum's Save dialog (found by 117's GUI run) opened another program's last folder instead of the panel's. Windows records, per program path, the first `lpstrInitialDir` it was ever given (`ComDlg32\FirstFolder`); a later dialog given that same folder opens in the program's last-used folder instead (`LastVisitedPidlMRU`, keyed by the file name). Other folders open as asked. Changing it would mean moving Checksum and `SplGetFileNameU8` to `IFileDialog::SetFolder` (not possible for PictView's hooked dialog).
evidence: specs/NEXT-WORK.md item 5, queue 104 entry 4 (L1842-1856 at 7993914c): measured by feature 121 - harness named `tandemcommander.exe` + probe row K0; `specs/121-small-batch/fix-log.md` and `research.md`; origin `specs/117-checksum-lists/`. Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §C *Decided - not to do* (L475, at 7993914c).
log: feature 121 measured the first-folder rule and left it as it was; its change was reverted

title: Checksum: an OEM-encoded list's accented names stay "missing"
reason: feature 117 (research E2), listed under NEXT-WORK §C Decided - not to do: OEM is never guessed - no signal tells an OEM list from a code-page list, so a guess would mis-read correct lists.
problem: Checksum decides a list's encoding once per file (mark, UTF-16 by NUL bytes, UTF-8 when the whole file is, else the code page). A list written in the OEM code page is read as the ANSI code page, so its accented names are reported "missing".
evidence: specs/NEXT-WORK.md item 5, the 117 entry (L1818-1841 at 7993914c): "an OEM list's accented names stay 'missing' (no signal tells OEM from the code page - a decision, 117 research E2)"; `specs/117-checksum-lists/research.md` E2; helper `src/common/salcsumlist.h`. Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §C *Decided - not to do* (L489, at 7993914c).

title: Is the missing shell copy hook (drag out of archives into Explorer) intended?
problem: The shell extension (`salext*.dll`, the copy hook used when dragging or copying out of archives into Explorer) is not shipped: its registration only runs if `utils\salext*.dll` exists (`src/salamdr1.cpp:4384-4398`), and the product ships neither DLL, so nothing is registered. Without it, the clipboard copy from an archive and its paste into Explorer are unreachable.
evidence: `specs/083-privacy-policy-winget/research.md` *Side findings*, F8 (withdrawn after T010; "whether the copy hook's absence is intended is a separate question"); `specs/085-privacy-defect-fixes/research.md` (end of file, open question); specs/NEXT-WORK.md item 7, F8 (L2075-2079 at 7993914c); `specs/160-drop-into-long-archive/fix-log.md` *Reachability* (the copy hook is the code-page `ICopyHookA` in `src/shellext/copyhook.c` and cuts the Explorer target at `MAX_PATH`). Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §C *Decided - not to do* (L497-499, at 7993914c).
notes:
Shipping the extension again would touch the installer and `PRIVACY.md` (what the installer writes), and needs the cross-binary DROPFAKE/CLIPFAKE fix that 069 left unconverted (item encoding-sites-069-chose-not-to-convert) plus 160's MAX_PATH findings in the copy hook.

Merged from `shellext-copy-hook-cuts-archive-target` (a-code-work part): Shell extension's copy hook cuts the Explorer target at MAX_PATH. Problem: Clipboard copy FROM an archive into Explorer needs the shell extension. Its copy hook is the code-page `ICopyHookA` and cuts the Explorer target at `MAX_PATH`, and the core cuts that target again (`mainwnd3.cpp` `tgtPath`, `DoPasteOperation` `pathBuf`). Evidence: Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §A item 12 (L325) (at 7993914c). specs/160-drop-into-long-archive/ (drop / paste INTO a 260+ byte archive done). At 7993914c: `src/shellext/shellext.h` ~138 (`ICopyHookA`), `src/mainwnd3.cpp` ~6175 `char tgtPath[MAX_PATH]`. Expected: If the extension is shipped again: a wide copy hook and a target that is refused, never cut. Notes: NW §C records an open question for the maintainer: is the missing copy hook (drag out of archives into Explorer) intended? (item 7, F8) - migrated by another part.
question: Is it intended that the product ships without the shell extension's copy hook, so that dragging or copying files out of an archive into Explorer is not supported?
options:
- A - intended: keep the shell extension out; record the limitation.
- B - not intended: build, ship and register `salext*.dll`; first fix its code-page `ICopyHookA` and `MAX_PATH` cuts (160) and the DROPFAKE/CLIPFAKE pair together with `copyhook.c` (069 §2 item 2); update the installer and `PRIVACY.md` in the same change.
